evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: The key object ('sponsors') and action ('view a list') have a single clear interpretation.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: The story clearly requests listing user profiles; no materially different interpretations are implied.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website for info and updates
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether this means a bulk email tool, a mailing list, a contact form, or automated notifications; 'for info and updates' is also unclear in scope.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: ‘Very clear map’ is subjective and can be implemented in materially different ways (interactive vs static, level of detail, labeling).

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself ... and links to slides
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what fields/actions are included in 'edit my training node' and what 'and links to slides' requires (add? edit? display? permissions?).

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'per day' refers to (calendar day, event day, training day) and what constitutes a 'registration' (training vs summit vs camp).

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status ... if attendend, refunded, no show
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous which statuses exist, how they are determined/updated, and what 'helps track' entails (view only vs edit/workflow).

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous how waitlisting works (automatic vs manual, per class vs global, ordering/priority, notification).

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what the 'cancellation terms' are (where defined, versioning) and when/where the checkbox is presented (registration, cancellation, both).

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: ‘Whatever workflow exists’ is undefined and allows materially different implementations; also unclear how deadline affects actions (block, warn, fees).

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: Conditional phrasing and undefined 'my schedule' behavior (bookmarking vs registration vs calendar export) create multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: The requested capability is clear: display the trainings the user is registered for.

evaluations.evidence: have a view ... shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: ‘All attendee information’ is ambiguous (which fields, privacy limits) and 'attached to their training node' can be implemented in different ways (tab, block, separate page).

evaluations.evidence: all trainee information is shown and can be filtered
evaluations.rationale: ‘All trainee information’ is ambiguous and could include different data sets; filtering requirements are underspecified beyond one example.

evaluations.evidence: possibly a map view ... skill level ... registrations remaining
evaluations.rationale: Terms like 'possibly a map view' and 'skill level' are underspecified; 'registrations remaining' could mean capacity minus confirmed, minus pending, etc.

evaluations.evidence: training options clearly marked
evaluations.rationale: ‘Clearly marked’ is subjective and allows materially different UI/UX interpretations despite listing fields.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page with an intro section ... and promote call for trainings
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'promote call for trainings' entails (banner, CTA, submission form link, messaging) and what content belongs in the intro section.

evaluations.evidence: have a link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: A homepage link to the training options list is a single clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Location and opening hours for the coding lounge are clearly requested.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether refunds are full/partial, single vs bulk, and whether it refers to Stripe API refund vs internal status only.

evaluations.evidence: become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what '$350 level sponsor' entails (benefits/role assignment, one-time vs recurring) and what 'sponsorships page' exactly contains.

evaluations.evidence: attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'associated with this company' means (employer field, sponsorship purchaser, email domain, manual linkage).

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'identify myself as' requires (company selection/creation, verification) and what constitutes the $350 sponsorship product.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Creating and maintaining venue records is clear at a high level without conflicting interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Viewing venue details is a clear action; the exact fields are not specified but the requirement is not materially multi-interpretable.

evaluations.evidence: sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous association chain (sessions by attendees who work for sponsor? attendees linked to sponsor page?) and what counts as a 'session' (talks, trainings, summits).

evaluations.evidence: payment page ... as the third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what the 'registration process' refers to (camp vs sponsorship vs training) and what the first/second steps are.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether assignment is one-to-many/many-to-many, what 'events' includes, and how featuring works on the sponsor detail page.

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: Listing the items sponsored by a sponsor is a clear requirement (given sponsor relationships exist).

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged for an individual sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: The action (enter payment info and charge card) for an individual sponsorship is clear.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'link' means (display list, associate accounts, invite attendees) and how attendees are selected/verified.

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Updating one's user profile is a standard, single-meaning capability.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Newsletter signup is a clear, commonly understood action.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts for consumption by Drupal Planet
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'for consumption by Drupal Planet' requires (specific taxonomy, RSS feed inclusion rules, metadata format).

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Creating blog posts is a clear action with no materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Reading the blog is a clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit that matches my brand
evaluations.rationale: ‘Matches my brand’ is subjective and can lead to materially different interpretations of filtering/matching/selection support.

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Summit registration is a clear action.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: ‘Detailed directions’ is subjective and could mean address only, step-by-step directions, map integration, transit/parking info, etc.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the summits the user is registered for is unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether the list includes contact details, export, filtering, and whether 'signed up' includes pending/cancelled registrations.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: ‘Basic information’ is undefined and can vary materially (title/description vs venue/time/speakers/requirements).

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing summit sponsors is a clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what constitutes an 'agenda' (sessions only vs timeslots, breaks, speakers) and required structure.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous how 'seats left' is calculated (capacity minus confirmed, minus pending, waitlist handling).

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: ‘Specific details’ is vague and can include many different information sets; not constrained by the story text.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: A list of all summits is a single clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: Providing information about sponsorship levels is clear at a functional level.

evaluations.evidence: WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what counts as 'all long-form content' (which content types/fields) and what qualifies as 'long-form'.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Adding a link from job listings to the sponsor profile is clear.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'learn about' includes (pricing, rules, steps) and who/what 'the sponsorship person' is (role, email, form).

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Posting a job is a clear action (create a job listing).

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the job board is a clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous relationship between room and location (room already implies location) and what a 'time slot' represents (session slot, training slot, duration rules).

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Viewing the schedule is a clear user-facing capability.

evaluations.evidence: final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'final' means (after all reviews? after schedule publish?) and what counts as 'sessions' (talks only vs including trainings/summits).

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous selection criteria and workflow effects of 'bulk approve' (which sessions, from what state to what state, notifications?).

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Setting a session's status to accepted is a single clear action.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'evaluated' means (scored, accepted/rejected, reviewed) and what form the notification takes (email, onsite message).

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous notification channel/content and what counts as successful submission triggering the notification.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Editing one's submitted session is a clear capability.

evaluations.evidence: register to speak at BADCamp, so that I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous whether 'register to speak' is separate from 'submit a session' (account creation? speaker profile?) or simply the submission itself.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session at BADCAMP
evaluations.rationale: Submitting a session for evaluation is a clear action.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: ‘Personalize’ is vague and could mean editing content, branding, layout, media, or adding modules—materially different scopes.

evaluations.evidence: list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'when they are' requires (date only vs date+time+timezone, multi-day ranges).

evaluations.evidence: offered several choices of idividual sponsorship on the second page of registration
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous what 'registration' refers to and what counts as 'several choices' (which options, pricing, selection rules).

evaluations.evidence: easily find a link in the menu
evaluations.rationale: ‘Easily find’ is subjective and can lead to materially different interpretations (menu placement, labeling, prominence).

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: Completing a user registration form to create an account is a clear requirement.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: ‘Session information’ is vague (which sessions, what details, search vs browse) and allows materially different implementations.
